content.text:
{
  "persuasion": "PERSUADED",
  "support_scope": "FULL",
  "rationale": "The supplied texts establish that sabbath names the complete structured seven (week/unit) crowned by its rest-member, at day-scale and year-scale alike. Parallel statutes equate ‘seven sabbaths’ with ‘seven weeks’; Greek idiom uses sabbaton for the week itself (‘twice in the sabbath,’ ‘one of the sabbaths’); and the law scales the identical unit to land-sabbaths and jubilee. This lexical and calendrical identification is more precise and explanatory of the cited mechanics than the common symbolic-rest reading, which accounts for the rest motif but leaves the counting, completeness, and multi-scale unit language under-explained. No material assertion printed in the entry is left unsupported by the evidence bundle.",
  "book_core_identification": "Sabbath names a complete seven crowned by rest—the week itself and the identical unit at every scale the law counts (days, years, jubilee sevens)—with rest as the completing member of that whole.",
  "book_secondary_elaborations": [
    "Hebrew counts ‘seven sabbaths’ (shabbatot) where Deuteronomy counts the same span as ‘seven weeks’ (shavuot).",
    "Greek calls the week the sabbath: ‘twice in the sabbath’ (dis tou sabbatou) = twice a week; every ‘first day of the week’ = ‘one of the sabbaths’ (mia sabbatōn).",
    "The rest is the completing member of the whole unit."
  ],
  "unsupported_glossary_assertions": [],
  "chapter_only_objections": [
    "The chapter’s reconstructed lunar-sabbath calendar (months of four sevens plus renewed-moon days) and its claim that the omer count functions as a checksum against continuous-week reckoning go beyond the glossary entry and are not required for its lexical identification.",
    "Typological extension of the unit to a 7000-year ‘great week’ and millennial sabbatismos, while using Heb 4:9, is chapter-level application rather than an assertion printed in the entry."
  ],
  "strongest_counter_interpretation": "Sabbath primarily and properly names the seventh day of sacred rest (creational, covenantal, and later christological/eschatological); any application to a full week or multi-year span is secondary metonymy or loose extension from the day that closes the period, and the dominant NT sense is fulfilled spiritual rest in Christ.",
  "counter_core_identification": "Sabbath = the seventh-day rest (literal or typological), with week/year usages derivative.",
  "counter_relation_to_book_core": "CONTRADICTS",
  "material_core_denial": "The counter denies that the word’s primary referent is the complete structured seven itself; it treats the unit-sense as secondary borrowing rather than the thing named.",
  "counter_case": [
    "Genesis 2:2-3 and the Decalogue repeatedly isolate ‘the seventh day’ as the sabbath of rest.",
    "Colossians 2:16-17 and Hebrews 3–4 are classically read as making the weekly institution a shadow whose substance is rest in Christ.",
    "Common Christian consensus (Responses A–D) centers the term on sacred/spiritual rest, treating calendar mechanics as secondary."
  ],
  "book_explanatory_advantages": [
    "Directly accounts for the double vocabulary of the identical omer command (Lev 23:15 shabbatot = Deut 16:9 shavuot).",
    "Explains why a sabbath can be ‘complete’ (temimot)—a predicate that fits a span, not an indivisible day.",
    "Fits the multi-scale usage without equivocation: sabbaths of years and seven sabbaths of years to jubilee (Lev 25).",
    "Matches unforced Greek idiom in which sabbaton simply means week (Luke 18:12; Matt 28:1 and parallels).",
    "Preserves the six-plus-one composition as definitional of the named unit rather than an incidental frame around a rest-day."
  ],
  "counter_explanatory_advantages": [
    "Aligns with the most frequent surface collocation of sabbath with cessation from ordinary labor and with later Christian rest-in-Christ typology.",
    "Requires no reconstruction of calendar mechanics beyond the continuous seven-day week familiar in most traditions."
  ],
  "evidence_book_core_cannot_explain": [],
  "comparative_winner": "BOOK",
  "decisive_sources": [
    "Lev 23:15 with Deut 16:9 (identical count under two names)",
    "Lev 25:2-8 (sabbaths of years / seven sabbaths of years)",
    "Luke 18:12 (dis tou sabbatou = twice a week)",
    "Matt 28:1 (mia sabbatōn = first day of the week)",
    "Heb 4:9 (sabbatismos as the remaining unit-rest)"
  ],
  "unresolved_objections": [],
  "confidence": "high"
}

support_scope.description: Support for the exact glossary BOOK ENTRY only, never for the supporting chapter as a whole.

book_secondary_elaborations.description: Secondary assertions actually printed in the glossary BOOK ENTRY; exclude chapter-only claims.

unsupported_glossary_assertions.description: Material assertions actually printed in the BOOK ENTRY that the evidence does not support. Must be empty for FULL and nonempty for CORE_ONLY.

chapter_only_objections.description: Objections to applications or arguments found only in the supporting chapter. Preserved for later chapter review and excluded from the glossary scope ruling.

instructions: Return only the requested structured result. Judge the exact glossary entry against the strongest specific alternative; treat the chapter as evidence, not as an additional judgment target.
